fields.h1: Build a Wellness Intake Form for Every Service You Offer
fields.hero_description: Build a wellness intake form that asks each client only the questions for the services they book, and keeps every answer.
fields.features_heading: What the Front Desk Knows Before a Visit
fields.features_subheading: Emergent builds a wellness intake form around the services you sell, with the screening questions each one needs.
fields.feature_1:
Services first, then their questions

The intake opens by asking which services the client is booking. A client who picks the sauna gets the sauna questions, and one who books a massage gets the massage ones.
fields.feature_2:
A booking that waits for a second look

Mark any screening question where a yes needs a staff decision. A yes holds that booking, and the app emails the manager that an intake needs review. The answer stays in the app.
fields.feature_3:
Ratings stored as numbers, not notes

Ask clients to rate areas such as sleep and energy from 1 to 10. Each score is saved as a number, so the same questions asked again at 90 days line up against the first answers.
fields.feature_4:
The waiver signed on the same form

Paste the waiver your center already uses at the end of the intake, followed by a typed or drawn signature. The app keeps each signature and its date on the client's record.
fields.feature_5:
One question per screen on a phone

Clients can fill out the intake on a phone in the lobby or at home, one question per screen. A long screening section stays easy to finish with a thumb, even on a small screen.
fields.feature_6:
Records in a database you own

Every intake lands in a database you own, with no response caps. On paid plans, export the code to your GitHub repository and host it wherever your records need to live.

fields.usecase_heading: Wellness Intake at Four Kinds of Business
fields.tab_content_1:
When the sauna and float are booked, their questions show

Coppergate Wellness House gives massage, sauna, and float tank their own screening sections. Fenella Vellacott books the sauna and the float and sees 2 sections, 9 questions. A yes to one sauna question puts that booking on hold, and Harlowe Jeske, the manager, gets an email that an intake needs review.
fields.tab_content_2:
In the last week, 3 missing intakes trigger a reminder

Beaumaris Retreat books 18 guests for each retreat, and its intake asks each guest to pick a morning session. Seven days before arrival, 15 had sent it: 8 for yoga, 4 for breathwork, and 3 for the trail walk. The other 3 got a reminder email that morning, and Ambrine Pellow planned the sessions from the counts.
fields.tab_content_3:
At 90 days, calm is the one score that dropped

New members at Breckridge Studio rate sleep, energy, movement, and calm from 1 to 10. At 90 days, the same 4 questions come back. Rafferty Lorne joined at 4, 5, 3, and 6 and answered 7, 6, 6, and 4. Calm fell 2 points while the rest rose, and Wynona Sabrann opens his review there.
fields.tab_content_4:
Which 2 of the 24 answers changed, marked at the top

Thistlecombe Wellness asks returning clients to update their intake once a year. A year after Cosimo Dandridge's last one, the app emailed him a link with his 24 answers filled in. He changed 2, his address and emergency contact, and Ilse Marwood sees both marked at the top of his record before his next massage.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Wellness Intake Form
fields.howto_description: Plan the services and screening questions for a wellness intake form, then build it with Emergent in seven steps.
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Name who reviews a held booking
fields.howto_step_1_des: List every service a client can book, such as massage, sauna, or float sessions. Each one becomes a choice at the top of the intake, and each choice opens its own section of questions.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Write the yes-or-no screening questions for each service with the person who leads your practitioners. Keep each one short, and mark the ones where a yes should put the booking on hold.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Pick four areas clients rate from 1 to 10, such as sleep and energy. Ask them again at 90 days in the same words. Identical wording keeps the first and second scores comparable.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Name the person who reviews held bookings, plus a backup for their days off. Their email says only that an intake needs review, and the answers stay in the app.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Place the waiver after the last question. Clients then sign with every other answer in, and they read its full text on the page instead of behind a link.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Put the services, screening questions, ratings, and reviewer into one prompt. Emergent builds the intake form, the database behind it, and a screen for staff. Change a question later by asking in plain English.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Submit one test intake that books two services, one with a yes on a screening question, and one from a phone. Check that the held booking reaches the reviewer and that the email carries no answers.

faq_plan.q: What is a wellness intake form?
faq_plan.a: A wellness intake form is the questionnaire a new client fills out before a first session at a spa or wellness center. It collects contact details and the services booked, with screening questions for each one. The practitioner reads it before the session starts.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a wellness intake form?
faq_plan.a: Decide which services clients book, write the screening questions for each, and name who reviews a yes. Describe all of it in one prompt to Emergent's AI form builder, which builds the form and the database behind it. Send yourself a test intake before you share the link.

faq_plan.q: What questions should a wellness intake form ask?
faq_plan.a: Ask for contact details and an emergency contact, then the services the client is booking. Give each service its own short screening section. Add a few ratings on a 1-to-10 scale, such as calm and movement, and close with your waiver and a signature.

faq_plan.q: Should one wellness intake form cover every service a center offers?
faq_plan.a: Yes, as long as each service gets its own section that opens only when it is booked. One intake keeps a client's contact details and waiver in a single record. A service that needs a long history of its own, such as needling, can still run a separate acupuncture intake form.

faq_plan.q: How long should a wellness intake form take to fill out?
faq_plan.a: Keep it short enough to finish in the lobby before the session starts. Show one section per booked service, with 4 or 5 questions in each. Leave anything the practitioner will ask in person off the form.

faq_plan.q: Can clients fill out a wellness intake form on their phone?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Send the link with the booking confirmation, and the intake opens in any phone browser. Emergent can build it as a conversational flow with one question per screen, and the answers reach the client's record before they arrive.

faq_plan.q: Should a wellness intake form ask about stress and mood?
faq_plan.a: Yes, as a simple 1-to-10 rating for calm, asked again at 90 days. Leave counseling questions out of a wellness intake. If your center also offers counseling, give those clients a separate therapy intake form written by the counselor.

faq_plan.q: Can a wellness intake form track a client's progress over time?
faq_plan.a: Yes, if it asks the same questions on the same 1-to-10 scale when a client joins and again at a set point, such as 90 days. Show both scores side by side and mark any that dropped. The app Emergent builds keeps every score in a database you own, and the comparison sits on the client's record.

faq_plan.q: Can clients sign a waiver on a wellness intake form?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Add a signature field under the waiver text. Clients can type or draw the signature on a phone or a front desk tablet, and it stays with that visit's intake.

faq_plan.q: How do returning clients update a wellness intake form?
faq_plan.a: Send them last year's answers already filled in and ask them to change only what is different. Mark each changed answer for the practitioner. A wellness center can do this once a year, and the same pattern fits a dental intake form updated at each checkup.
